evidence.title: Nvidia’s Rebound, Falling Oil And A Strong Dollar: Three Signals Complicating The Fed’s December Decision
evidence.body: [e002:f01] Thorne, Chief Market Strategist at Wellington Altus, believes Huang’s reinstatement and falling energy prices have brought some stability to markets, which warrants a rate cut in 2027. [e002:f02] Markets have been volatile over the past few weeks as the leadership turmoil in Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and rising oil prices have kept investors on their toes, with eyes keenly focused on inflation and what it means for the upcoming Federal Reserve policy decision. [e002:f03] However, on Monday, Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO, President, and board member of the chipmaker, along with a recent pullback in oil prices amid growing supply, has given new wind to markets, sending benchmark indexes higher. [e002:f04] Despite the recent turn of events, markets are overwhelmingly predicting a rate hike from the Fed in December, as investors and experts believe inflation will remain a concern. [e002:f05] Why Ed Yardeni Thinks The Fed Should Raise Rates By 50 Bps Ed Yardeni, economist and president of Yardeni Research, said in an interview with CNBC that the market reversal following Huang’s return may be a “one-day wonder” as other issues still weigh on the economy. [e002:f06] The economist said that there is “certainly” a 25 basis-point hike on the cards; but he believes the Fed should hike rates by 50 bps. [e002:f07] He noted that while expectations of a rate hike have fallen, actual inflation numbers are steadily at 3% year-over-year, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh “has pounded the table” about wanting it at 2%. [e002:f08] Meanwhile, data from the CME FedWatch tool puts the probability of a 25 bps rate hike in December at 96.4%, while the odds of a 50 bps hike are at 3.6%. [e002:f09] Robin Brooks, Senior Fellow in Economic Studies at the Brookings Institution, said in a post on X, “The fly in the ointment of yesterday's risk rally is that the Dollar kept rising. [e002:f10] Thorne said that he believes the Fed can tighten without raising rates by holding benchmark rates at 3.75% to 4% and “let the real rate do the work.” He cited declining oil and gasoline prices, lower PCE inflation expectations and recent market changes for his stance. [e002:f11] However, Fed meeting minutes released on Tuesday show that a majority of regional Fed bank boards favored lifting rates ahead of the central bank's late-October policy decision. [e002:f12] Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed’s preferred gauge for inflation, is scheduled for release on Wednesday. [e002:f13] October headline PCE price index to rise 3.8% year-over-year and core PCE to increase 0.3% month-over-month, according to a Bloomberg survey. [e002:f14] At the time of writing, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) , which tracks the S&P 500 index, fell 0.25% overnight. [e002:f15] One user said, “$SPY The Fed is nuts to raise rates now. [e002:f16] What is needed now is to push oil prices lower and to drop the inflationary tariffs first. $QQQ.” Another user said, “Everything is selling off now not because AI anymore but because tomorrow last important data for Dec FOMC and looks like we can’t escape hikes, we probably could repeat 2018, dec rate hike and tank all the way till Christmas And then bounce $SPY big drop.” Meanwhile, the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was flat amid ‘neutral’ sentiment.

evidence.title: Money Talks: Beginning in 2027, the Fed is Offering a Strong Incentive to Sign Up for FedNow
evidence.body: [e003:f01] [Image 1](https:// Whether your credit union is exploring instant payments, already receiving them or ready to grow send volume, a new[Federal Reserve](https:// could make 2027 an important time to take the next step. [e003:f02] 1, 2027, Federal Reserve Financial Services will offer a discount program for eligible new and current FedNow Service participants. [e003:f03] For credit unions, the incentive is an opportunity to look at where you are today and where instant payments could take you next. [e003:f04] Two incentives, two ways to move forward The program includes a FedNow Receive Discount and a FedNow Send Discount. [e003:f05] Credit unions may qualify for one or both if they meet the applicable requirements. **Receive: Up to a $20,000 Incentive** Credit unions enabling FedNow receive may qualify for a one-time statement credit. [e003:f06] The credit begins at $5,000 for institutions that enable FedNow instant payment receipt. [e003:f07] To be eligible for the FedNow Service receive credit, institutions must also participate in specified Federal Reserve Financial Services offerings, as specified by the Federal Reserve. [e003:f08] For credit unions that have not yet implemented FedNow, the incentive provides another reason to evaluate whether now is the right time. **Send: Up to $80,000 Incentive** For credit unions ready to enable or expand FedNow send, the opportunity is potentially even greater. [e003:f09] Qualifying send-enabled institutions can receive up to $20,000 for enabling FedNow send and meeting certain transaction thresholds. [e003:f10] The maximum incentive can $80,000 for institutions also participating in the FedACH Receipt Discount Program. [e003:f11] The $20,000 tier requires at least 100 completed qualifying FedNow send transactions per month while the maximum $80,000 tier requires at least 2,500 per month. [e003:f12] Existing senders already meeting the applicable threshold may instead qualify by increasing average monthly FedNow send volume by at least 50%. [e003:f13] The new incentive specifically rewards qualifying institutions that meet applicable send-volume requirements or, for existing senders already at those thresholds, significantly increase volume. [e003:f14] It’s finding payment experiences that solve real problems for members. **Look Beyond the Incentive** Up to $20,000 for qualifying receive institutions and up to $80,000 for qualifying send institutions will naturally get attention. [e003:f15] Our solution supports the FedNow Service and the RTP network, with capabilities including 24/7/365 liquidity, dedicated subaccounts for reconciliation and connectivity with core and digital banking platforms. [e003:f16] Find your starting point Wherever your credit union is today, now is the time to start planning for 2027.

evidence.title: 米国総合PMI、4カ月ぶり低水準の54.6に低下 物価圧力と供給網の混乱が受注を圧迫
evidence.body: [e004:f01] 米国の企業活動の伸びは11月に4カ月ぶりの低水準に鈍化した。 [e004:f02] S&Pグローバルの速報値によると、米国総合PMIは10月の55.9から54.6に低下し、高い生活費がサービス業の受注を抑え、能力制約が生産を抑制した。 [e004:f03] 製造業指数は54.5、サービス業は54.7に低下した。 [e004:f04] S&Pグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフ・ビジネス・エコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は、調査はなお第4四半期の実質GDP成長率が年率換算で約3%になることを示しており、雇用ももう一段の力強い雇用統計に沿った内容だと述べた。 [e004:f05] 投入コストの上昇は鈍化したが、調査の物価指標はなお、向こう数カ月のインフレ率が米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の2%目標を大きく上回る状態と整合的だと報告書は指摘した。 [e004:f06] 米国の民間部門の活動は11月、4カ月ぶりの低い伸びとなった。 [e004:f07] 生活費の高止まりと能力制約が受注と生産を抑えたが、調査はなお傾向を上回る経済成長を示している。 [e004:f08] S&Pグローバルによると、製造業とサービス業を追跡する米国総合PMI生産指数の速報値は、今月54.6となり、10月の確定値55.9から低下した。 [e004:f09] 製造業指数は54.9から3カ月ぶりの低水準となる54.5に、サービス業指数は56.1から4カ月ぶりの低水準となる54.7に低下した。 [e004:f10] サービス業の新規事業は減少し、工場の新規受注はほぼ横ばいだった。 [e004:f11] 指数（11月速報値） 11月 10月 総合生産 54.6 55.9 製造業 54.5 54.9 サービス業活動 54.7 56.1 注：50を上回る水準は拡大、50を下回る水準は縮小を示す。 [e004:f12] S&Pグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフ・ビジネス・エコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「11月は生産の伸びが鈍化したものの、最近の数値は印象的に力強く、PMI調査はなお第4四半期のGDPが年率約3%で成長することを示している」と述べた。 [e004:f13] 国内総生産（GDP）は第3四半期に年率3.4%で成長し、個人消費と人工知能（AI）インフラの急速な整備に支えられた。 [e004:f14] これは受注を満たすことへの企業の懸念を強め、基調的な物価圧力を押し上げる可能性が高い。 [e004:f15] 英国では民間部門の成長が2カ月ぶりの低水準となる52.3に鈍化したが、予想を上回った。 [e004:f16] 製造業生産は27カ月ぶりの高水準に上昇した。

evidence.title: 米国の生活費は2027年も上昇の恐れ、物価・金利・食費・公的支援縮小・家賃の5要因
米国の生活費は2027年も上昇の恐れ、物価・金利・食費・公的支援縮小・家賃の5要因
evidence.body: [e006:f01] 見直しの対象は、低所得者向け公的医療保険のメディケイド、医療保険制度改革法（ACA、通称オバマケア）に基づく民間保険の加入制度、高齢者などを対象とする公的医療保険のメディケアに及ぶ。 [e006:f02] 制度変更は段階的に実施され、メディケイドの受給資格審査に関する措置の一部は2027年から始まる。 [e006:f03] 食料購入を支える公的給付も縮小した。 [e006:f04] 米公共放送PBSが2026年10月に報じたところでは、低所得者の食料購入を助ける「補助的栄養支援プログラム（SNAP）」の給付を失った人は500万人を超える。 [e006:f05] ■（5）賃貸住宅の供給増による家賃の抑制効果が弱まる 住居費は何年にもわたり米国の物価を大きく押し上げてきた。 [e006:f06] ただ、賃貸住宅の供給が急増したことで家賃の値上がりは抑えられ、借り手が家主に家賃などの条件を普段より交渉しやすい状況が生まれていた。 [e006:f07] 家主は引き続き費用の増加に直面する。 [e006:f08] 利上げに伴う資金調達費用に加え、光熱費、保険料、税金も上がり、賃貸経営の利益が圧迫される。 [e006:f09] 不安をあおるために、生活費の負担増を列挙したわけではない。 [e006:f10] 今後どの費用が増えそうかをできる範囲で把握し、家計への打撃を避けるために取れる対策を講じてほしい。 [e006:f11] Erik Sherman 前へ 1 2 次へ 2 / 2ページ。

evidence.title: Cleveland among the Fed regional boards that sought to raise rates in October
evidence.body: [e007:f01] Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack has been at the forefront of calling for rate hikes. [e007:f02] Eight of the Federal Reserve’s 12 regional bank boards recommended raising the so-called discount lending rate prior to the Federal Open Market Committee’s October meeting, at which policymakers kept their benchmark rate unchanged.
